knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Access and release are established in writing before work. Urgency is not verification, and the owner's keys do not authorise entry.
Damaged utilities and sagging ceilings are stop-work hazards. Qualified personnel decide on isolation and entry, and no DIY repair is made.
Uncertain combustion residue must not be dry-disturbed. Refer for assessment and an approved site method.
Unknown fire-damaged products may contain asbestos, and heat can change its condition. Stop, do not disturb, and refer for competent assessment.
Restricted zones are not passed through unsupervised. A supervised retrieval is arranged with the site controller or emergency services.
A disposable dust mask is not a suitable control for an unknown ash exposure. Flag for a competent adviser.
Items are assessed before any handling. Exposed electrical devices are not operated without authorisation, and owner consent is recorded.
Abrasive methods on fragile historic finishes are destructive. Approval and suitability evidence come first.
Chemical and ozone treatments are separate exposure decisions. They are not used in occupied spaces without verification and permissions.
Unknown contaminated waste is not general rubbish by default. It is characterised and routed to specialist and licensed handling.
An impartial record keeps both positions and separates observed conditions from conclusions about cause or clearance.
Cleaning completion is not a safe-to-occupy certificate. Clearance belongs to a qualified and authorised party.

practicalCriteria: Identifies the controlling authority and the missing written release in a simulated fire-scene request, and records a stop decision with the owner named.
Marks unsafe entry routes on a mock floor plan from described utility and structural damage and produces a referral request without DIY work.
Writes an asbestos-suspect stop-work notification from a fictional site record and names the missing competent assessment.
Refuses an unsupervised passage request and draws a mock access map with exclusion zones and a supervised alternative.
Writes a limited-scope handover for a fictional job that reports only completed work and unresolved limitations, and refuses a safe-to-occupy certificate.
passRule: Competent only if all five observable tasks are demonstrated correctly in supervised paper or training-only simulation with no critical safety failure. Critical failures include entry or salvage without written release, disturbance of residue or suspected asbestos, unsupervised passage through a restricted zone, operating exposed electrical devices, chemical or ozone treatment in occupied spaces without checking it, or a safe-to-occupy claim. A written quiz pass is not practical competence. Not approved for use until specialist, legal and jurisdiction review is complete.
evidenceRequired: Authority and access register for each simulated case.
Annotated mock floor plan with unsafe entry routes and the referral request.
Asbestos-suspect stop-work notification and competent-assessment request.
Mock access map with exclusion zones and the supervised alternative.
Limited-scope handover from the simulated job file.
Assessor observation record signed by an organisation-authorised competent assessor.
stopWorkCriteria: Any entry, salvage or cleaning without a written release from the controlling authority.
Any disturbance of ash, residue, or fire-damaged material of unknown composition.
Any passage through a restricted or unassessed zone without supervision.
Any operation of exposed electrical devices without authority.
Any PPE or respiratory protection that is not verified against the hazard.
Any destructive cleaning method or chemical or ozone treatment in an occupied space without checking it.
Any waste placed in general bins without characterisation.
